Sunflower Pediatric Clinical Trials (SPeCTr) | v2025.09

SPeCTr was founded in 2016 with KUMC investigators receiving NIH funding to participate in the first cycle of National Institutes of Health Environmental Influences on Child Health Outcomes IDeA States Pediatric Clinical Trials Network (ECHO ISPCTN). SPeCTr was awarded funding for the second cycle of the ECHO ISPCTN for the period of September 2020 through August 2025 and applied for the third cycle of funding in April 2024, which will carry work forward to 2030. The NIH ECHO Program has two major components, the ECHO cohorts — for observational research, and the ECHO IDeA States Pediatric Clinical Trials Network — for intervention research. While Kansas does not have a cohort site, it is a very active site in the ISPCTN. The goals of the 18 state clinical trials ISPCTN network include providing medically disadvantaged and rural populations with access to state-of-the-art, rigorously conducted clinical trials, building pediatric research capacity and supporting the professional development of faculty-level pediatricians and their support teams in the conduct of clinical trials research. Descriptors of the network and organizational structure have been widely published, as have outcome studies from specific studies, many of which have been led by the KUMC team. All components of the NIH ECHO program focus on five key health areas including pre-, peri-, and postnatal, upper and lower airway, obesity, neurodevelopment, and positive health. Since inception, the SPeCTr network has conducted over 10 multi-site trials across disadvantaged states and populations, with one of the only rurally focused primary care trials. SPeCTr has also developed a vast online repository of trainings that are free on their website and designed for faculty and staff interested in pediatric clinical trials conduct, including the ability for any research team member across Kansas to ask for immediate “Peds Clinical Trials Help” via the SPeCTr website (https://ksspectre.org). Another SPeCTR strength is training junior investigators who are pursuing NIH funding as a Principal Investigator. At least 18 investigators have reached this milestone with the help from training resources, team meetings, and in-depth mentoring from the senior research team, including pediatricians located in rural areas.

Teaching & Learning Technologies | v2022.04 | Point(s) of Contact: Philip Wilhauk

The Teaching & Learning Technologies (TLT) department provides faculty, staff, students, and the community with leadership and support for the successful integration of new and existing educational technology into KUMC learning environments – both in the physical learning spaces and online. TLT is made up of five teams: Faculty Support/Online Learning, Learning Systems, Media, Learning Spaces, and Testing Services. The Faculty Support/Online Learning team includes three School Liaisons each with a background in instructional design as well as two Online Learning Specialists. Learning System Support includes four system administrators who maintain TLT’s core online systems supporting teaching and learning including Blackboard, Panopto and Saba. TLT Media supports classroom audio/visual technology, provides event AV support, and facilitates video conferencing (ITV) connecting the Kansas City, Wichita, and Salina campuses. They also offer video production and editing services. Testing Services manages the 200+ seat Computerized Testing Center (CTC) in Dykes Library and also provides support for online testing and bring-your-own device testing in the classroom. The Learning Spaces team manages the operation and scheduling of KUMC’s centrally scheduled classrooms and courtyards.

Transgenic & Gene Targeting Institutional Facility | v2022.04 | Point(s) of Contact: Melissa Larson

The Transgenic and Gene Targeting Core is an animal and cell genetic model development and research facility that supports transgenic and gene-targeting research endeavors, promotes technology development, and serves as a resource for these technologies. Our facility provides "3D" service for design, development, and depository of mouse and cell models for KUMC researchers and collaborators at other academic institutions. The Facility consists of a Transgenic Rodent Core, a Stem Cell Core, and a Molecular Biology Core. Services include pronuculear injections, blastocyst injection of ES cells, cell culturing and mutagenesis, and molecular biology services in CRISPR reagent design, targeting vector construction and genotyping. The Facility consists of three full time technical staff (one PhD level, one MS level, and one BS level), along with faculty oversight. The Facility has the necessary equipment and space for a range of front-end embryo manipulation and cell culture. Laboratory space consists of three rooms in the Hemenway Life Sciences Innovation Center (HLSIC G020, 558 ft2; HLSIC G022, 496 ft2; and HLSIC G024, 110 ft2). HLSIC G020 is the main laboratory for animal surgeries, embryo manipulation, and molecular biology procedures; HLSIC G022 consists of a suite of three interior rooms dedicated to various pluripotent stem cell culture, and G024 serves as a cryopreservation laboratory. Equipment includes:

  • Two embryo microinjection stations-
    • Nikon Eclipse Ti-U microscope equipped with DIC, HMC and fluorescence, Leitz manipulators, an Eppendorf Cell Tram air micrometer, a SAS air syringe, and an Eppendorf Femtojet.
    • Nikon TE2000 inverted microscope with Nomarski optics and temperature-adjustable warming/cooling stage is equipped with Narishige manipulators, a Narishige micrometer, a SAS air syringe, and a Femtojet. This microscope is also equipped with a Piezo drill and an XY Clone laser objective for zona drilling.
  • Injection needle station- A de Fonbrune microforge, a Kopf vertical pipette puller, and a Sutter P-97 horizontal puller for making holding and injection pipettes.
  • Pluripotent stem cell culture stations- Two Biosafety cabinets dedicated to stem cell culture; three Sanyo MCO-18M tri-gas incubators- BioRad GenePulser II electroporator for the transfection of DNA into cells.
  • Other equipment- includes two stereo and tissue culture microscopes with video and high-resolution camera capabilities; a controlled-rate freezer for embryo cryopreservation; an auto-fill liquid nitrogen storage tank and a vapor shipper.
  • Molecular Biology Equipment- Two Eppendorf Mastercycler PCR thermocyclers, gel electrophoresis units, and a Bio-Rad GelDoc Go Gel Imaging System.

School of Health Professions (SHP) | v2025.09

Established in 1974, the School of Health Professions (SHP) at KUMC is one of the largest schools of allied health sciences in the United States. More than 300 clinical affiliation sites in the U.S. and abroad establish the SHP as a leader in international collaboration in health sciences and offer our students the opportunity to gain experience in rural, urban, and international health care settings. The SHP has academic programs in over ten fields ranging from certificate to doctoral degrees with nearly 800 baccalaureate and graduate students. Five of the SHP graduate programs are ranked in the top 15 nationally. Research activities within the SHP reflect the range of its programs. In FY24, total research funding was ~$25 million from a variety of funding agencies including the NIH, Department of Education, Department of Defense, and non-profit foundations. This funding level places the school within the top 15 in NIH funding for schools of health professions. The SHP leadership are fully invested to develop and support research by providing resources including space, pilot funding, travel, training, and research support infrastructure.

Dietetics & Nutrition | v2025.09 | Point(s) of Contact: Debra Sullivan

Dietetics is the science of managing food and nutrition to promote health. Registered dietitians are food and nutrition experts who provide nutritional services in hospitals, schools, nursing care facilities, and other institutions. These essential healthcare professionals are responsible for developing food and nutrition programs to prevent and treat illness or promote general dietary health. The Department is chaired by Dr. Debra Sullivan, the Midwest Dairy Endowed Professor. The Department offers several certificate and degree programs in the fields of dietetics and nutrition, including a Master of Science in Dietetics and Nutrition and a PhD in Medical Nutrition Science. Students with degrees in nutrition or biological sciences have the opportunity for clinical and translational research at a world-class academic health center renowned for its research facilities. This program emphasizes training in the core sciences of nutrition, biochemistry, biostatistics, and the most advanced research methodology.

Nutrition Assessment Laboratory

This 1,500 ft2 laboratory includes six fully equipped offices for study coordinators and post-doctoral fellows, 10 student workstations, a conference room, and a room for participant counseling via telephone. This laboratory maintains 10 licensed copies of the Nutrition Data System for Research (NDSR) software (updated annually), access to the freely available NCI supported Automated Self-Administered 24-hr (ASA24®) Dietary Assessment Tool, and access to the Nutrition Literacy Assessment Instrument App (NLit). Equipment includes: three Veggie Meters® (Longevity Link Corporation), a non-invasive device which uses reflective spectroscopy to measure skin carotenoid content to validate self-reports of fruit and vegetable intake, three Jamar hand dynameters, two Omron automated blood pressure machines, and a bioelectrical impedance analysis machine.

The Nutrition Literacy Laboratory

This 300 ft2 space, located in the Wescoe building, includes workspace and computers for three research assistants, equipment for collecting anthropometrics, a play space for children, sink and cabinets for storage and a conference table and chairs. University password protected laptops, and 2 iPads are available from the lab for offsite data collection purposes. The Nutrition Literacy Assessment Instrument (NLit) has been registered for copyright by the Dietetics & Nutrition department, and the University of Kansas.

Nutrition-Development Laboratory

This 3,500 ft2 facility, located in the Smith Center, is dedicated to research on infants, toddlers and children. This laboratory includes an assessment room with all necessary equipment for measuring weight, height (stadiometer), length (length boards), head circumference (non-stretchable tapes), and blood pressure; six coding stations for coding videotapes of infant behavior; 4 rooms with a total of 7 stations for testing infant/child behavior; a family waiting room with a lactation room for breast feeding mothers; a refrigerator and microwave; reception areas; storage areas for files and other items; student/staff offices each equipped with telephone and computer; a conference room that accommodates 20-24 people for regularly scheduled staff meetings; and a business center equipped with telephones, laser printer, fax, and copy machine. Data stored on the KUMC network can be accessed from any of these dedicated work areas.

Dietetics and Nutrition Basic Science Laboratories

The department's basic science laboratories are in Breidenthal Hall, a free-standing health sciences building on the main KUMC campus. The two laboratory offices (rooms 1029 and 1033) for research staff and students. The offices are equipped with computer and software systems needed. There are three wet laboratories (room 1010, 1011 and 1012).

Biomarker Laboratory

This laboratory is located in rooms 1011 and 1012 of Breidenthal Hall, and features a dedicated laboratory workstation, plus equipment that supports a wide array of biological and biochemical assessments. The wet laboratory houses an Agilent 7890B gas chromatograph system, two refrigerated centrifuges, 2 tabletop centrifuges, blood processing equipment, a lab fume hood, two -80°C freezers, a specimen refrigerator, a N-EVAP nitrogen evaporator, and a UV transilluminator.

Microbiome Laboratory

This space features dedicated laboratory workstations (in room 1012 Breidenthal) and equipment that supports a wide array of biological and biochemical assessments. The wet laboratory encompasses houses a QIAcube Connect DNA/RNA extraction system, one tabletop centrifuge, blood processing equipment, a lab fume hood, two -80°C freezers, two -20°C freezers, refrigerator, spectrophotometers/fluorimeters, 96 well plate reader, two analytical balances, and PCR instruments.

Nutrition Unit and Metabolic Kitchens

The Nutrition unit of Clinical Translational Science Unit includes an 830 ft2 metabolic kitchen and a 600 ft2 demonstration kitchen. The metabolic kitchen is a fully equipped professional grade kitchen used to provide standardized meals required by study protocols. The demonstration kitchen, which contains seating for 24, is a fully equipped kitchen with installed cameras and audiovisual aids to provide high class cooking skills and nutrition education programming.

Occupational Therapy Education | v2025.09

The Department of Occupational Therapy Education’s innovative research strives to impact the health and occupations of people and their communities. KU faculty are leading efforts in community-engaged research to support full participation of individuals with diverse strengths and challenges in everyday life. Within our department we have faculty advancing research and patientcare. The Accessible Leisure Laboratory research team investigates factors impeding or facilitating leisure participation and the effect of physically active recreation on health behaviors and body composition. The Borrell Laboratory assesses the brain after injury and uses this information to drive rehabilitation. The Borrell lab is located within the Human Performance Laboratory at the Landon Center on Aging. Faculty in the Department also provide clinical services and support research through the Driving and Mobility Clinic in the Laboratory for Advanced Rehabilitation and Research in Simulation to use state-of-the-art, high-tech virtual reality equipment to advance mobility outcomes and promote rehabilitation and health. Other prominent research foci include: 1) how to minimize frailty and fall-risk in people living with chronic diseases with an emphasis on exercise and physical activity interventions, 2) how to increase evidence-based service access for families of children with autism spectrum disorder and other related disorders using telehealth technology, 3) investigating sensory experience and intervention promoting participation in everyday life, and 4) the development and implementation of innovative educational methodologies and community participation outcomes of stroke survivors.

Physical Therapy, Rehabilitation Science, & Athletic Training | v2025.09

The physical therapy program at the University of Kansas is ranked 6th out of public programs in the nation. The department is within the School of Health Professions which is ranked 11th in NIH funding for comparable schools. The faculty of the Physical Therapy and Rehabilitation Sciences department participates in research that utilizes the department’s resources as well as those of affiliated programs. The Dean of the School of Health Professions and the Chair of the Physical Therapy Department are fully invested in the development and support of research by providing resources in the form of space, pilot funding, travel, and training, and research infrastructure support.

School of Medicine (SOM) - Kansas City | v2025.09 | Point(s) of Contact: Jenni Mandala

The KU School of Medicine has enjoyed a longstanding reputation for training physicians who excel in their knowledge of medicine and delivery of expert health care. Eight years ago, our curriculum was redesigned using an interdisciplinary, patient-centered model, incorporating a strong clinical foundation into the basic sciences, and facilitating development of exceptional critical thinkers who can analyze problems, formulate effective plans of action, and provide optimal clinical care. Active, self-directed learning is encouraged through a variety of teaching tools, including small group discussions, problem-based learning, electronic procedure simulators, virtual microscopy labs, and standardized patients. The different learning styles of adults are further accommodated through tablet computers and podcasting. As the nation faces a serious shortage of practicing physicians, new medical schools are being developed, and existing medical schools are exploring ways in which they can increase the number of physicians graduated each year. To this end, the KU SOM has expanded programs in Salina, Kansas and Wichita, Kansas. The core basic science content (years 1 and 2) is identical to that of the Kansas City campus with the benefit of additional opportunities for early patient care experiences that will enhance learning in the basic sciences. While curricular requirements are the same on all three campuses, the Salina campus focus is on delivery of health care in rural and secondary care centers. The KU-Wichita campus focus is on primary-care medicine in community-based hospitals, and the Kansas City campus offers the full range of clinical opportunities available to students studying in an academic, tertiary health-care center. Student resources, support services and enrichment opportunities (e.g., electives, research, and international study) are similar across all three campuses.

Anesthesiology | v2025.09

The dynamic specialty of anesthesiology has witnessed unprecedented growth and change since the administration of ether in 1846. Today the field has evolved into a continuum of perioperative care beginning with the presurgical assessment and education of the patient through intraoperative management to the postoperative phase. The KUMC Department of Anesthesiology Is committed to training physicians to become outstanding, competent, and compassionate anesthesiologists. The structure of the training program encourages the development of residents in a supportive environment allowing them to incorporate the skills and knowledge needed to provide the best possible care to their patients. The extraordinary faculty have great breadth in their variety of interests and depth in their specific areas of focus. The Department strives to create an engaging and challenging experience with the incorporation of didactic lectures and hands-on experience in a wide range of clinical settings along with cutting-edge simulator-based education. The Chair of the Department of Anesthesiology is dedicated to building a world-class pain research program with a burgeoning Pain Research Center. This has included hiring several new faculty members.

Biochemistry & Molecular Biology | v2025.09 | Point(s) of Contact: Liskin Swint-Kruse

The mission of the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (BMB) is to offer a dynamic research environment in these disciplines, provide a superior educational experience for graduate students and medical students, develop a rich training environment for postdoctoral fellows, and contribute service to the institution and community. Research in BMB is focused on elucidating the molecular mechanisms that underpin both normal biological processes and human diseases. Areas of strength include the regulation of gene expression, maintenance of genome integrity, cell signaling, proteostasis, characterization of membrane proteins, medical applications of protein evolution, and structure determination via X-ray crystallography and cryo-electron microscopy. Faculty members are associated with several cross-disciplinary centers across the university.

Biostatistics & Data Science | v2025.09 | Point(s) of Contact: Megan Tremblay

The mission of the Department of Biostatistics & Data Science is to provide an infrastructure of biostatistical, bioinformatics, informatics, and data science expertise to support and enhance the research, service, and educational needs of the University of Kansas Medical Center (KUMC). There is approximately 7,000 square feet of office space within the KUMC Department of Biostatistics & Data Science, which includes a conference room, various offices, equipment and services such as computers, copiers, faxing, overnight mailing and portable display cases. There are 26 Ph.D. Biostatistics Faculty, 7 M.S. Biostatisticians, 14 Informatics Specialists, 2 Project Managers, 2 Administrators, 1 Administrative Assistant. Our faculty members are active researchers collaborating and consulting in research projects and initiatives throughout the Medical Center, in addition to pursuit of their own research agendas and participation in curricular instruction. Expertise in the department includes linear, nonlinear, and longitudinal modeling, clinical trial and experimental design, survival analysis, categorical data analysis, robust statistics, psychometric methods, Bayesian methodology and statistical genomics. Our innovative MS and PhD programs were created to help meet the ever-increasing demand for biostatisticians and data scientists needed to take leadership roles in careers as researchers and educators in academia, government and industry. The course work, seminars and collaborative research experience have been designed so that our graduates acquire the knowledge and expertise that allows them to work at the frontier of their field.

The Department of Biostatistics & Data Science has invested over $1M toward hardware since 2009 to enhance the informatics and biostatistical computing abilities. All computers in the Department of Biostatistics & Data Science are connected to a 10 Gigabyte per second local area network that provides more than 100 Terabytes of network file storage. Networked file servers offer continuous hardware backups of stored data through mirrored storage systems, along with daily tape backups. Weekly tape backups are stored off-site for additional protection of research data. The network is managed by KUMC’s Information Resources who provide installation, training, and maintenance on all information systems. The Department of Biostatistics & Data Science local area network is connected to a switched, 10 Gigabit Ethernet backbone that provides high-speed Internet access through the KUMC Internet2 communication network. Currently, KUMC’s Internet2 access is via the Kansas Research and Education Network (KanREN). KanREN supports Internet2 connectivity for all of its members via a 10Gbps link to the Great Plains Network (GPN), and KUMC is connected to KanREN via a 1 Gigabit per second connection. This high-speed network provides each workstation with access to the World Wide Web, electronic mail, electronic file transfer, and shared CD-ROM-based databases. There are also three informatics software engineers housed in the same office suite as the PI. As in the past, these personnel are available to the PI to answer unanticipated programming questions.

The Department of Biostatistics & Data Science is home to six NIH-funded cores that are directed or co-directed by Department faculty and four additional cores that Department faculty and staff have affiliations with. Departmental resources such as: administrative support and project management, computing resources, physical space and facilities, faculty & staff, and access to specialized statistical, bioinformatics, and computational biology software are shared across all cores. This is both a cost-effective and practical solution given the nature and similarity of the services provided by each of the cores. All personnel will have access to a variety of standard statistical packages such as SAS, R, Minitab,StatXact, S-PLUS, and STATA; sample size and power computation applications such as nQuery and Pass 2021; and numerous other resources as detailed in the sections that follow. The Department also maintains and routinely updates copies of a variety of molecular databases and numerous scientific software licenses for general use, and custom software development is available when existing software does not meet investigator needs.

Cancer Biology | v2025.09 | Point(s) of Contact: Stefan Bossmann

The Department of Cancer Biology at the University of Kansas Medical Center is a basic science department committed to understanding the fundamental mechanisms of cancer to inform novel therapeutic and preventive strategies. Researchers in the department focus on areas such as cancer cell biology, tumor microenvironment interactions, and the molecular and genetic bases of cancer progression. The department emphasizes translational research, aiming to bridge laboratory discoveries with clinical applications to reduce cancer incidence and mortality. Additionally, it plays a pivotal role in educating the next generation of cancer researchers and clinicians through rigorous graduate programs and interdisciplinary training.

Cell Biology & Physiology | v2025.09

The research programs in this department, which include cellular and integrative physiology, neuroscience, reproduction/development, and cancer, involve all levels of analysis from genes to whole animal behavior. Together, these programs aim to define biological function in health and disease. Total NIH funding for faculty in this department was $6.3 million in 2023, ranking 19th nationally in research funding among all public university physiology departments, and 31st among the 127 public and private medical schools. Under the direction of the current Chair, Gustavo Blanco, MD, PhD, the Department continues to build research capacity.

Family Medicine & Community Health | v2025.09

In response to rapidly shifting dynamics in healthcare access and delivery across the state of Kansas, the Family Medicine and Community Health (FMCH) department at KUMC has remained at the forefront of bridging healthcare gaps for rural and underserved communities. With a philosophy rooted in integrating clinical care and community health, FMCH recognizes the critical challenges patients face initiating and navigating healthcare. Through innovative workforce strategies, such as deploying Community Health Workers (CHWs), and rigorous implementation science, FMCH is driving scalable, evidence-based solutions that connect community needs with clinical care and inform policy. This unique approach leverages decades of experience and strong partnerships to address healthcare access issues while expanding its reach through primary care, research, and community health initiatives. By meeting people where they are, combined with FMCH’s ongoing commitment to adaptability, collaboration, and access for all ensures that FMCH fills critical gaps and advances healthcare delivery and outcomes across Kansas.

►
FMCH Clinical Operation | v2025.09

The main FMCH clinic at KUMC provides comprehensive care, addressing a wide range of patient needs, including preventive, acute, and chronic care integrating a diverse team to ensure holistic care. FMCH also operates multiple clinics across the Kansas City metro area, including the Medical Pavilion, Landon Center on Aging, Arrowhead, KU MedWest, Prairie Village (Village Office Center), ICA-1/Executive Health, and ICC/Sports Medicine. These locations expand access to care and cater to the unique healthcare needs of various communities within the region. FMCH ensures services and education are accessible in other regions of Kansas by having clinical and training presence in Wichita, Salina, and southeastern Kansas. FMCH’s expansion plans include a significant merger with Olathe Health, further increasing the organization’s footprint and services across the state. FMCH strengthens its presence in the community through partnerships with local Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) and clinics, such as Vibrant Health, Mom Clinic, JayDoc Free Clinic, and BullDoc Health Clinic. These efforts provide vital healthcare services to uninsured populations, with FMCH faculty members also playing significant roles in public health initiatives helping guide public health initiatives in our area’s two most heavily populated counties, Wyandotte and Johnson counties.

FMCH Research Division | v2025.09

Department of Family Medicine and Community Health-Research Division (FMCH-RD). This growing division is housed within three separate areas of the KU Medical Center complex. The research division occupies a 2,400-ft2 office suite within the KUMC Endowment Building. The Division has eight full-time faculty investigators with experience in conducting health research. The Department now ranks within the top ten Family Medicine departments in the U.S. in NIH funding according to the Blue Ridge Institute for Medical Research. Four research division faculty members also maintain clinical practices. All research division staff have been hired with the intent of building a translational health program studying cancer and chronic diseases. These staff have expertise in health informatics, community-based participatory research, participant recruitment, and biospecimen collection. The research division houses and runs the community engagement program for the new KUMC Clinical and Translational Science Award, Frontiers.

FMCH Primary Care & Community Networks | v2025.09

FMCH is deeply engaged in providing expertise and experience to several primary care networks (e.g., COPE Network, and DARTNet Institute) that play crucial roles in accelerating the movement of scientific discoveries into practical applications that benefit patients, communities, and the healthcare system, particularly in rural areas of Kansas. FMCH’s network engagement began over two decades ago with the founding of the Kansas Patients and Providers Engaged in Prevention Research (KPPEPR) at KUMC, one of the first networks in the nation to foster partnership among clinicians, patients, public health professionals, community organizations, and academic researchers. KPPEPR's research activities include projects such as KANSURVIVE, the KU Cancer Center/Masonic Cancer Alliance Rural National Cancer Institute Community Oncology Research Program (NCORP), rural melanoma education, and the Treating Pain with Acceptance and Commitment Therapy Trial (T-PACT Trial). Its mission is to conduct collaborative, interdisciplinary community-based research aimed at promoting health through prevention, behavior change, early diagnosis, and treatment. Through networks, FMCH serves as an authority for implementing evidence-based interventions and community health initiatives statewide.

FMCH Communities Organizing to Promote Equity (COPE) Network | v2025.01

The rapidly growing COPE Network is the backbone of several interconnected programs aimed at addressing health gaps in rural Kansas. The COPE Network initiative focuses on empowering communities to identify and tackle local health issues through a network of community-based Regional Project Managers, Community Health Workers (CHWs), and Local Health Equity Action Teams (LHEATs) comprised of local civic-minded community members. Building on this foundation, KDHE partners with the COPE Network to support local organizations in areas such as organizational development, developing reports, and procurement of funding (i.e., recent successful efforts have led to funding supporting local projects and sustainability of the COPE Network). Currently, KDHE has tasked the COPE Network with the State Health Improvement Plan (SHIP) Health Literacy Survey to enhance data collection in populations across Kansas. KDHE has also tasked the COPE Network with facilitating a community health coalition grant program. Together, these programs illustrate the COPE Network's growth and its multifaceted benefits, including a trained easily mobilized research and implementation network, improved access to health and social services, enhanced community engagement, and stronger, data-driven public health interventions tailored to the needs of rural populations.

►
FMCH Community Health Worker Network (CHW-Network) | v2025.09

The CHW-Network is also housed in FMCH. The CHW Network is a highly sought resource providing collaborative development to entities across the state, nation, and world exemplified by current CHW-Network collaborations noted below:

  • K-State 105 Rural Health Practice / Rural Ag Health CHW Project: The CHW Network works with K-State Health Extension (KSRE) to train and deploy CHWs in rural Kansas, focusing on farming communities’ unique health challenges and connecting them to medical resources.
  • Facts Not Fear Health Education (Wichita): The CHW Network supports training for CHWs to deliver accurate, evidence-based health education in Wichita, addressing misinformation and improving health literacy.
  • Mental Health Association of America Co-Training: The CHW Network partners with MHA to co-train CHWs on supporting behavioral health needs in communities, equipping them to connect individuals to resources and care.
  • KDHE Interpreter Training: The CHW Network collaborates with KDHE to train CHWs as healthcare interpreters, improving language access and care for non-English-speaking patients.
  • Job Readiness for CHWs with Asian Women for Health (Boston): The CHW Network participates in a job readiness initiative that prepares CHWs with skills in outreach, care coordination, and support.
  • Public Health Improvement Grant (PHIG): The CHW Network supports PHIG efforts to develop and expand the CHW workforce across Kansas by designing training programs and strengthening local public health infrastructure.
  • COPE Network: lead hiring and implementation of 60 CHWs across 20 counties.
  • San Juan Bautista Hospital (Guatemala): The CHW Network trains CHWs and hospital administrators in the work of CHWs.
The CHW-Network originated through collaborative work with the COPE Network, supporting the professionalization and integration of 60 CHWs across both rural Kansas counties beginning in 2021. Recognizing CHWs' critical role in addressing social determinants of health (SDOH) the CHW-Network grew to focus on professional tailored business solutions. The CHW-Network currently leads efforts to support and expand CHW programs across the state, serving as the go-to resource for training, workflow design, and program implementation. Through comprehensive 40-hour training modules, tailored consulting, and innovative technology solutions, the network equips organizations with the tools needed to successfully launch, integrate, and sustain CHW initiatives.

Internal Medicine | v2025.09 | Point(s) of Contact: Ilse Duarte, Miranda Handke

The Department of Internal Medicine focuses on providing outstanding clinical service to patients, exceptional medical education for medical students, residents, and other health professionals, and a commitment to translational research to expand the frontiers of biomedical knowledge. The Department has invested in scientific endeavors that result in life-saving medical breakthroughs and accelerate the translation of innovative research into better healthcare. The Department of Internal Medicine is composed of 15 various divisions and over 600 faculty members – physician scientists, researchers, and clinical faculty leading the clinical and research enterprise in multiple areas. Several faculty members are national and international leaders in their area of specialization. With over 150 active awards and contracts, the Department averages $42M in annual federal funding with over 250 active clinical trials and registries.

Endocrinology, Diabetes, & Clinical Pharmacology Division | v2026.03

The Endocrinology, Diabetes, and Clinical Pharmacology Division brings together researchers and clinicians from multiple disciplines to further understand and treat diabetes and musculoskeletal disease. Research grants involve hyperlipidemia, hypertension, diabetes, post menopause and obesity. Faculty research efforts focus on diabetes mellitus and osteoporosis, both of which have significant impact on nutrition, obesity, and metabolism research. The division facilitates multidisciplinary approaches to support and grow early-to-midcareer investigators in nutrition and obesity. The division facilitates multidisciplinary approaches to support and grow early-to-midcareer investigators along with being the home division of the KU Diabetes Institute and the Cray Diabetes Self-Management Center.

Gastroenterology, Hepatology & Motility Division | v2026.03

Faculty and staff use the most advanced diagnostic and therapeutic tools available to ensure the best results for each patient. The division also has dedicated staff that includes technologists, nurses, nutritionists and others meeting patient's needs with the quality of care and compassion expected from a leader in the field. The division encompasses a broad range of investigators and research topics. Geriatric Medicine Division | v2026.03 | Point(s) of Contact: Bruce Troen

Geriatricians at KUMC work to meet the person-centered goals of older adults for all their health, using evidence-based models of care with the goal of maximizing a person’s functional independence and seeking additional support when needed. Clinical activities are in force across the whole continuum – hospital, clinic, skilled nursing facilities, long-term care, and the patient’s own home – with interprofessional methods that include partnerships with therapy, pharmacy, social work and community services. All care is driven by the 4Ms:

  • What Matters – We seek to know each patient’s specific health outcome goals and care preferences
  • Mobility – We work to maintain a patient’s mobility and function, as well as prevent and treat the complications immobility
  • Medication – We optimize medications to reduce harm and burden while maximizing benefits
  • Mentation – We perform evaluations for and manage dementia, delirium, depression and other factors affecting a person’s cognition

Aging demographics present a significant burden to healthcare systems of the United States that is poised to worsen dramatically in the next decade. Aging is the predominant risk factor for many co-morbidities including cancer, cardiovascular disease, kidney disease, and cognitive decline. Geroscience focuses on the biology of aging as a major contributing factor to chronic diseases, functional capacity, and healthspan in older adults. Identifying strategies to slow the aging process are critically needed to improve healthcare outcomes and quality of life for older adults. Towards this goal the division of Geriatrics embeds a “cells-to-community” approach that aligns scientific approaches, from pre-clinical to human clinical and community trials, in a structured framework that focuses on the concepts of frailty and resilience. Current research examines potential lifestyle modifications to enhance healthspan, including minimal exercise strategies, nutritional supplementation, countering inflammaging, and other approaches to enhance functional and cognitive function during aging. Ongoing interventional trials involving older adults include short session high intensity interval training, supplementation with nicotinamide riboside (a form of vitamin B3), or bright light therapy to improve circadian rhythms as potential interventions to improve function capacity, cognitive performance, and even sleep quality. Additionally, the pipeline includes pre-clinical trials examining the impacts of vitamin D supplementation, nicotinamide riboside, sleep disturbance, on mouse frailty and cognition. Cellular studies investigate the underlying hallmarks of aging including the role of epigenetics (including biologic versus chronologic aging), mitochondrial dysfunction, and stem cell exhaustion. Together, these projects unite to lay a foundation for advancing cutting edge technologies to develop potent future interventions to meet the needs of aging populations.

Medical Informatics Division | v2026.03 | Point(s) of Contact: Diego Mazzotti

Medical Informatics serves to design, implement, and evaluate informatics solutions that serve physicians and patients. Faculty provide informatics expertise to support translational and clinical researchers and other health professionals at the University of Kansas Medical Center, as well as affiliated and partner organizations. Dedicated to developing innovative informatics solutions, including data science, natural language processing, artificial intelligence and machine learning, to support and accelerate translational and clinical research. Faculty have expertise in big data analysis, utilizing electronic medical records (EMR), claims, behavioral, proteomic and genomic data with a clinical focus that includes, but is not limited to, outcomes and health services research, economic evaluation in medicine, sleep medicine, diabetes and kidney research and pharmacoinformatics.

Medical Oncology Division | v2026.03

The National Cancer Institute-designated comprehensive cancer center, University of Kansas Cancer Center and the Midwest Cancer Alliance Rural NCI Community Oncology Research Program (KUCC-MCA Rural NCORP) leverages over 45-years of experience as a Southwest Oncology Group Cancer Research Network member, 20-year experiences providing oncology care via telemedicine, a 15-year history of successfully conducting research in rural primary care settings, and a 10-year experience opening and running clinical trials within rural health care networks—all supported by KUCC expertise in partnering with rural oncology and primary care practices to accomplish our goals. The clinical trial program is highly active with numerous investigator-initiated clinical trials. These trials evaluate novel agents and therapeutic strategies in efforts to improve the treatment of all types of malignancies; to improve the results of allogeneic and autologous stem cell transplantation. Our clinical investigators are leaders in the development of many Phase II and III cooperative group clinical trials; some have led to changes in practice and the standard of care of several malignancies.

Nephrology & Hypertension Division | v2026.03

Multidisciplinary academic program whose priority is basic, clinical, translational research leading to improvements in the care of patients with kidney disease and hypertension. The nephrology program was ranked among the top 50 nationally by U.S. News & World Report for 11 years and ranked 38th in 2020. Faculty clinicians are involved in both routine and advanced care and contribute to the formal Nephrology Fellowship training program. Division investigators lead laboratory-based and clinical studies exploring mechanisms of renal disease, blood pressure regulation, and related pathology, often in collaboration with the Jared Grantham Kidney Institute which includes 42 faculty, 23,000 sq ft of state-of-the-are laboratory space and more than $7 million per year in research funding. The Kansas PKD Research and Translation Core Center (RTCC) was awarded a five-year NIDDK grant to advance PKD science and serve as a magnet to attract highly competitive researchers and physician scientists to lead to a cure.

Physical Activity & Weight Management Division | v2026.03 | Point(s) of Contact: John Jakicic

The Division of Physical Activity & Weight Management conducts research to promote physical activity and nutrition for the prevention and treatment of overweight and obesity and related comorbidities in children, adults, and special populations. Additionally, this division supports the University of Kansas Weight Management Programs that provide a medically supervised weight management clinic that also serves as a clinical research site. Four laboratories (two each at the University of Kansas Medical Center (KUMC) and University of Kansas-Lawrence) and an administrative site (at the KUMC Endowment facility) are directed by Dr. Joseph Donnelly, and Dr. John M. Jakicic. The division uses energy balance approaches and behavioral strategies in laboratory and out-patient research and clinical programs. A whole-room calorimeter provides state-of-the-art measures of energy expenditure and substrate utilization. Given the rural nature of Kansas, the division is active in the development of techniques for remote delivery of interventions and data collection. The faculty in the division have an outstanding record of past and current support for graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, and junior faculty.

Research Laboratory in the Fairway North Building

This new ~20,000 ft2 facility opened in September 2024 approximately 1.5 miles from the main campus in the Fairway North Building. This building is adjacent to the KUMC Clinical and Translational Science Unit (CTSU) – Fairway facility, which will facilitate collaboration between these entities to support research. The division moved some research operations to the Fairway North facility in December 2023 (exercise training, cardiometabolic exercise testing, DXA, etc.), with expanded and full renovation complete in September 2024. This facility includes participant reception and waiting area, staff offices and workstations, 3 clinical examination rooms, a DXA room, 2 cardiometabolic testing rooms, 1 resting metabolic testing room, strength testing facilities and equipment, functional testing facilities and equipment, supervised exercise training facilities and equipment, blood collection and processing area, biospecimen storage, media filming and editing rooms (to allow for remote media interventions), wearable technology facilities (actigraphy, other remote monitoring), conference rooms with audiovisual capabilities, and secured data storage.

KUMC Energy Balance Laboratory and Clinical Weight Management Program (Kirmayer Building)

The division’s Energy Balance Laboratory and Clinical Weight Management Program is located within Kirmayer Fitness Center and occupies 5,000 ft2 This location just completed an ~$1,000,000 renovation in April 2024. This facility includes participant waiting area, staff offices and workstations, 6 clinical exam rooms, 2 consultation rooms, DXA room, metabolic testing room, blood collection and processing area, additional testing area for function testing, strength testing, a remote exercise delivery area, and conference room with audiovisual capabilities.

Pulmonary, Critical Care, & Sleep Medicine Division | v2026.03

The Pulmonary, Critical Care and Sleep Medicine division has a robust program of clinical investigation, with interests in sepsis, pulmonary hypertension, cystic fibrosis, interstitial lung disease, asthma, hemodynamic monitoring conditions, and sleep. The division has doubled in size in recent years, in both the number of faculty and the number of fellows in the program. The division boasts the largest Adult Cystic Fibrosis Center in the Midwest. It is also nationally certified as a center of excellence for multiple conditions: pulmonary hypertension, pulmonary fibrosis, lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM), and primary ciliary dyskinesia syndrome. Our ACGME accredited Pulmonary Critical Care Fellowship Program has a 100% board pass rate for all boards over the past five years. All our fellows are active in clinical research and present their work at national meetings. The Division is also responsible for administration of the Medical Center's Zamierowski Institute for Experiential Learning, the region's premier simulation education center. We oversee curriculum development and execution of simulation education for the School of Medicine, the School of Allied Health, the School of Nursing, the University of Kansas Health System, and the Graduate Medical Education program.

The Department of Microbiology, Molecular Genetics and Immunology conducts high-impact research that is relevant to human health and trains the next generation of biomedical scientists and physicians to advance the understanding of infection and immunity in ways that benefit humankind. The Department occupies 20,000 square feet of lab and office space on four floors of the University of Kansas Medical Center basic science complex. The Department houses several research core facilities: X-Ray Crystallography Core, Protein Expression and Purification Core, Flow Cytometry Core, Genome Sequencing Facility, Microarray Facility, Electron Microscopy Facility, Gene Targeting and Transgenics Facility, Histology Imaging Analysis Core, Integrative Imaging, and the Bioinformatics Core. The department is also home to three laboratories: Drs. Lutkenhaus, Zucket, and Tse.

Neurology | v2025.09

U.S. News & World Report ranked the Neurology & Neurosurgery department as the 26th best program in the country, placing it in the top 50 for the 13th consecutive year. The department’s 55 neurologists provide world-class neurology care for people living with complex conditions of the brain, spine, and nervous system. Department divisions emphasize clinical focus and include a Cognitive Neurology Division founded in 2004 and has grown consistently since then. Currently, the Cognitive Neurology division includes 11 faculty members who have developed a critical mass of research that has grown to $11.9 million in annual NIH funding in 2023.

Obstetrics & Gynecology | v2025.09

The Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology is dedicated to excellence in patient care, education, and research. The department offers comprehensive training programs, including residency and fellowship opportunities in areas such as gynecologic oncology, maternal-fetal medicine, and academic specialist training. Research efforts focus on advancing innovation in people’s health, with ongoing projects, educational outreach, and specialized research initiatives like the Hull Body Composition Laboratory, which conducts innovative research in nutritional sciences, including the investigation of factors affecting body composition in all stages of life. Laboratory space dedicated to body composition assessment across the lifespan is in the Smith-West buildings on the KUMC campus. This space includes offices for research assistants and the following equipment: a DXA (GE Prodigy), BodPod, PeaPod (infants up to 10 kg), bioelectrical impedance analyzers (Tanita, TBF-400, Bodystat Quadscan 4000), and all equipment required for assessments of height, body weight, skinfolds, body circumferences and sagittal abdominal diameter. The department also provides high-quality patient care through The University of Kansas Health System, ensuring comprehensive services for reproductive health.

Pediatrics | v2025.09

The Department of Pediatrics provides access to patient care, medical education, and clinical research to residents in all 105 counties of the state of Kansas. The Department includes more than 60 providers (pediatricians, psychologists, nurse practitioners, etc.) who provide the full range of primary care and some specialty services to children across the state as part of the University of Kansas Health System. The pediatric practices are designated as Patient-Centered Medical Homes by the National Committee for Quality Assurance (NCQA). The pediatric practices serve over 24,000 unique patients per year, with over 65,000 visits across our many locations. In addition to teaching medical students and residents, many of our faculty also engage in federally funded research with strong senior faculty for child development, health services and outcomes, rural health, pain, obesity and feeding. The department has 48 active awards in FY24 totaling almost $45 million in funding.

Population Health | v2025.09 | Point(s) of Contact: Simon Lee

The Department of Population Health was created in 2019 as a merger of the Departments of Health, Policy and Management and Preventive Medicine and Public Health. The Department of Population Health, located in the KUMC School of Medicine, provides a robust, interdisciplinary research environment in an academic medical center setting. The only department of the School that holds faculty and programs on all three campuses of the University of Kansas Medical Center (Kansas City, Wichita and Salina), Population Health is focused on improving health and reducing health inequities for all people in Kansas and beyond. This rapidly expanding department includes 38 PhD and MD investigators with expertise in cancer prevention and control, health disparities, healthcare delivery and redesign, quality of care, nicotine addiction, nutrition, obesity, cardiovascular diseases, and health policy and health behavior. Our multidisciplinary faculty has experience in a broad range of research methodologies including secondary data analysis of large datasets, quality improvement intervention and measurement, economic evaluation, program evaluation, health services, clinical trials, epidemiology and surveillance, behavioral intervention, community-based participatory research, and qualitative research. The department is home to four graduate degree programs – Master of Public Health, Masters in Health Service Administration, Master of Science in Clinical Research and a PhD in Health Policy and Management. The Department also hosts two centers – Juntos! Center for Advancing Latino Health and the Implementation Science Equity Center of Biomedical Research Excellence (NIGMS-funded COBRE). Departmental extramural research funding totaled more than $10.2 million in FY 2023, reflecting a mix of federal, state, corporate, and private foundation contracts and grants.

The team of administrators in the Department of Population Health works hard to create a collaborative environment with plenty of opportunity for constructive feedback and collaboration among faculty members. Through multiple community-based research alliances (e.g. Masonic Cancer Alliance, NCI-designated University of Kansas Cancer Center, Juntos! Center for Advancing Latino Health) the department has a long tradition of support for community-based research and evaluation activities and encourages early-stage investigators to establish such relationships to address community and public health needs. The Department is able to provide faculty members with administrative support solely for the purpose of grant preparation and separate from day-to-day administrative support.

On the Kansas City campus, the Department occupies over 16,000 ft2 of office and research space. Faculty have individual, private offices centrally located on the main campus of the KUMC School of Medicine and near supportive administrative and information technology staff. These dedicated office spaces include computer and laptop access, with password protection and automatic logoff when left unattended. This includes analytic software (e.g. Dedoose, SAS, etc.) and compliant privacy/security practices that support use of the CCW Virtual Research Data Center (i.e., broadband internet, Google/Microsoft browsers, newest Windows operating systems, VMware Horizon Client) and other restricted access datasets.

Psychiatry & Behavioral Sciences | v2025.09

Members of the Division of Research, Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences are engaged in basic and clinical studies, as well as translational research of genetic factors contributing to mental illness, psychiatric and behavior disorders (e.g., alcoholism, addictions, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, autism, eating disorders, obesity, Prader-Willi, Alström and fragile X syndromes). The Division of Research provides an environment for clinical and basic science investigators to engage and carry out research activities to investigate the causation of a wide range of neuropsychiatric disorders leading to therapeutic interventions. The mission of the Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences crosses many disciplines including translational research involving basic sciences and clinical domains within the Department and fostering close connections with other Departments at the medical center and graduate schools to provide a framework to support a variety of research areas and scientific expertise.

School of Medicine (KUSM-W) - Wichita | v2025.09

KUSM-W, established 50 years ago, educates tomorrow’s physicians and health care leaders through community partnerships to improve the health of Kansans. KUSM-W plays a central role in educating young physicians, graduating more than 50 physicians per year, with more than half staying to practice in Kansas. Ascension Via Christi Hospitals Wichita, Inc., Wesley Medical Center, and the Veterans Affairs Medical Center together offer a combined licensed-bed capacity of more than 3,000, where students can participate in the care and supervision of patients. The KUSM-W campus, strategically located in the heart of the city, features 11 academic departments, 13 administrative departments, 14 accredited residency and fellowship programs, 130 administrators and support staff, with 111 full and part-time faculty with a reputation for excellence in teaching. The medical school also boasts nearly 700 volunteer faculty who lend their skills to the students’ educational experience. Between 1975 and 2022, KUSM-W graduated 2,437 medical students, and 2,515 resident graduates between 1988 and 2022. The KUSM-W’s physical structure consists of two conjoined buildings that total 128,186 ft2.

SOM-Wichita Information Technology Services | v2025.09

Information Technology Services (ITS) is the central University organization responsible for the planning, installation, operation, support, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the campus voice, data and video networks at the KUMC School of Medicine, located in Wichita, Kansas City, and Salina. IT Services provides campus faculty, students, and staff with information, resources, and services in support of computing technology needs, research and education. Services provided include a centralized Help Desk staffed by internal employees, storage of user data on network file servers, workstation support, connectivity, and other specific services as needed, including SQL database hosting and redundancy planning/implementation for mission critical projects.

Laptops used for university business are required to have Computrace asset recovery software installed and are required to be full disk encrypted using McAfee’s Endpoint encryption product. University policies disallow sensitive information from being stored on personal computing devices and unencrypted mobile devices. Protection for virus, phishing, and other security threats is accomplished on several levels, including firewall protection, Intruder Prevention System. Workstations are protected by McAfee AntiVirus/phishing/malware product, as well as McAfee SiteAdvisor browser-based protection. Microsoft Software Update Service is used to ensure that all Microsoft updates are applied to all Windows servers and workstations.

KUSM-W - Farha & Dykes Libraries | v2025.09

The George J. Farha Medical Library on the University of Kansas School of Medicine–Wichita campus carries over 15,000 volumes of books and subscribes to more than 250 publications. Faculty and staff are able to use all of the Farha Medical Library services. The library features comfortable reading areas, a computer lab with a networked printer, and study rooms with table, chairs, computer and networked printer. The lab computers provide access to the internet, email, the MS Office 2007 Suite, EndNote, and statistical software (EPI Info, SAS, and SPSS). The Farha Library collection includes 70 current print journal titles, 13,000 electronic full text journal titles, and 2,899 monographs. The monograph collection is supplemented with electronic collections such as AccessMedicine, MDConsult, and UpToDate, which provide full text access to many medical textbooks and information. In addition to PubMed, major databases such as CINAHL, PsycINFO, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and others are available. Electronic journals and products are available to clients both on- and off-campus.

There is direct access to the A.R. Dykes Library of the Health Sciences, which has 51,067 unique eJournal subscriptions, 11,428 unique eBooks, and access to e-journal titles, e-books, and 100 research databases, 24/7. The Farha library works cooperatively with the main campus Dykes library (located at the KU Medical Center in Kansas City). The Farha library also belongs to state, regional, and national library networks which facilitate location and borrowing of materials. Reference and interlibrary loan/ document delivery services are very responsive to client needs.

School of Nursing (KUSON) | v2026.02

For over 120 years, the KU School of Nursing (KUSON) has built a reputation for nursing leadership and excellence. The KUSON has been dedicated to preparing students for the challenges that await them upon graduation. The first class to complete their nursing education at KUSON was comprised of just four young nurses. In 2025, the KUSON enrolled 540 students. Founded as the Department of Nursing in 1906, the KUSON exemplifies responsiveness to healthcare needs through innovative education, nationally recognized research initiatives, and professional activities. As the flagship nursing school in Kansas, we have two campuses—Kansas City and Salina—and we partner with eight community colleges to provide additional educational opportunities for students who choose to remain in their home community while pursuing a bachelor's degree. The KUSON has been a National League for Nursing Center of Excellence in Nursing Education in three consecutive periods, 2012-2027 and is also home to the Kansas Nursing Workforce Center.

The nursing baccalaureate program, established in 1929, enrolled 403 students in 2025. KUSON was approved to offer the state’s first Master of Science in Nursing, direct entry degree. This pre-licensure master’s is designed specifically for those with an existing bachelor’s degree who now want to become an RN. The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Nursing program was established in 1983 to meet the demand for nursing researchers to study relevant clinical problems. Graduates are prepared to conduct independent research and scholarship in nursing; generate and expand the theoretical, empirical and philosophical bases for nursing practice; provide leadership to the profession; and interpret nursing to society. In 2025, 24 students were enrolled in the KUSON PhD program. The Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP), established in 2008, prepares advanced practice nurses at the highest level of nursing practice. The DNP offers sophisticated, cutting-edge experiences that help nurses actively engage in a complex, dynamic, and demanding healthcare field. Skills in collaboration, innovation, and evaluation, complemented by advanced practice nursing skills, prepare nurses to shape the future of healthcare.

KUSON Office of Grants & Research (OGR)

The OGR provides services to facilitate the research and the scholarly activities of the faculty in the KUSON. The KU
